We need to evaluate according to the five criteria (though they listed 5, but earlier said check exactly four things, but they list 5 items; we must check all). Determine if answer is acceptable.

1. SCOPE: Estimand: mean baseline biomarker value across all patients. Population: all patients in trial, one row per patient. Units: ng/mL. The analyst removed -999 sentinel rows (QC failures) and deduped to one row per patient (keeping highest sample_seq). This matches population definition: all patients, but they excluded patients with sentinel -999 (i.e., missing baseline). The contract says "The data contains sentinel values (-999) that are not valid measurements". So those should be excluded. So the mean should be over all patients with valid baseline measurements. The contract says "The mean is over all patients, not all rows". It doesn't explicitly say to exclude missing values, but sentinel values are not valid measurements, so they should be excluded. So scope is correct.

2. GROUNDING: The numeric claim 50.46 ng/mL matches printed mean 50.4627808988764, rounded to 2 decimals. Evidence lines are present. So grounded.

3. OVERREACH: No causal claim, just descriptive mean. So fine.

4. UNACKNOWLEDGED DATA PROBLEMS: Any other issues? The data dictionary mentions assay_batch unit error only for biomarker_final, not baseline. So fine. They accounted for sentinel and duplicates. No other missing data. So no unacknowledged problems.

5. FALSE PREMISE: Premises to verify: baseline values are in ng/mL (true per data dictionary). Mean over all patients not rows (they did). Data contains sentinel -999 (true). Data contains duplicate patient rows (true). So premises hold. No false premise.

Thus answer seems sound. Verdict accept.
